 8 weather alerts in effect When to expect showers and thunderstorms across the Phoenix area this weekend 
 A Flash Flood Watch is out for metro Phoenix, and much of the state will be under flood risk by Sunday. For the Valley, 1-2” of rain is likely through Sunday. By Royal Norman Published : Oct. 29, 2026 at 5:36 AM MST | Updated : 12 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PHOENIX (AZFamily) — One strong storm system moving into the Pacific Northwest is going to give us at least two waves of potentially heavy precipitation.
 While we are not forecasting the type of severe weather we had last week, complete with confirmed tornado touchdowns, we are focusing on the chance for flash flooding across the state. 
 A Flash Flood Watch is out for metro Phoenix, and much of the state will be under flood risk by Sunday. For the Valley, 1-2” of rain is likely through Sunday.
 The first wave is due Friday morning and will persist through much of the day. Expect showers and thunderstorms with locally heavy rain. A severe storm is not out of the question. 
 By Friday night, we expect the first wave to move out of Arizona and bring us a relatively quiet Friday night into Saturday afternoon. However, the second wave could begin as early as Halloween night (Saturday), so we can’t give the all-clear for the trick-or-treaters.
 Download the First Alert Weather App That second wave should increase during the nighttime hours and last much of the day on Sunday. Expect clouds, scattered showers and some embedded thunderstorms around the entire state Sunday. At present, Sunday is looking like a bigger rain day than Friday, but that forecast is just beginning to come into high relief.
 High temps will generally be in the 70s for the weekend but it’s possible we’ll see some afternoon temperatures in the 60s on Sunday.
